Latest News — September 17, 2026
September 17, 2026 — The National Hurricane Center has completed its reanalysis for the 1971–1975 Atlantic Hurricane Seasons. More than 3,000 tweaks/changes were made, including some big ones.
  • EDITH 1971 downgraded from 160 mph C5 to 150 mph C4.
  • GINGER 1971 upgraded from 110 mph C2 to 115 mph C3, now a major hurricane.
  • Removal of 5 tropical depressions in the 1971 season.
  • DAWN 1972 downgraded from a 80 mph C1 to a 65 mph TS.
  • CHARLIE 1972 upgraded from a 70 mph TS to a 90 mph C1.
  • Removal of 2 tropical depression in the 1972 season.
  • DELIA 1973 upgraded from a 70 mph TS to a 85 mph C1.
  • TD (AL20) upgraded from 30 mph to a 70 mph TS.

Data across the TROPICAL CYCLONE DATABASE is powered by the Atlantic Hurricane Database (HURDAT2, 1851–2025) for all landfall positions, wind, and pressure. The database was also utilized to recover landfalls HURDAT2 didn't flag. A landfall counts if a storm’s center crosses a coastline at tropical storm strength or above. This website is built as a reference and educational tool, so as always, confirm figures/decisions against the National Hurricane Center’s official reports.
